question: Should maintainers accept the terminal production-hook proof plus regression tests as sufficient for this session-state/message-delivery boundary, or require a live two-agent compaction run before merge?
rationale: The patch is focused and source-backed, but the original bug is timing-dependent user-visible duplicate delivery and the proof stops at production-hook terminal evidence rather than an end-to-end live interaction.

options.title: Land with scoped proof
options.body: Accept the existing terminal production-hook proof and focused regression tests as enough for this narrowly applied fallback filter.

options.title: Request live two-agent proof
options.body: Ask for a real two-agent compaction recovery run showing one delivered reply and preserved safe source context before merge.

options.title: Pause for boundary/API review
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want replay safety handled at a broader delivery API or side-effect boundary instead of the compaction fallback filter.

recommendation.title: Land with scoped proof
recommendation.body: Accept the existing terminal production-hook proof and focused regression tests as enough for this narrowly applied fallback filter.

likelyOwner.reason: The history sample points to steipete as the strongest current-main owner for compaction and inter-session runtime boundaries.
